capabilities.contract: An equivalent CapsWord action exists on all three OSes
capabilities.windows: caps_word resolves to the Windows state toggle.
capabilities.macos: capsword is the explicitly declared equivalent; actual generated/control and catalogue owners exist.
capabilities.linux: caps_word resolves to the actual shortcuts manager session toggle.
capabilities.basis: Shared actions.toml explicitly maps caps_word and capsword as equivalents while retaining a separate macOS Karabiner implementation; action-ID differences are not missing whole features.

capabilities.contract: Repeated invocation of the advertised action has an explicit behavior
capabilities.windows: The generic action toggles; the AltGr producer has the separately confirmed pre-clear defect.
capabilities.macos: The catalogue action requests ACTIVE again; generated native-key on/off manipulators are a different origin.
capabilities.linux: The catalogue action toggles the same active session.
capabilities.basis: Observed local action contracts; no common product decision requiring toggle or idempotent enable for all origins was found. The macOS catalogue handler is not equated with the separate physical CapsLock graph.

capabilities.contract: Capitalization is owned by the desktop CapsLock level
capabilities.windows: State owner requests SetCapsLockState from CapsWord or genuine user lock intent.
capabilities.macos: Actual graph emits CapsLock; catalogue completion requests true via KeyState.
capabilities.linux: Manager locks through actual Hook/capture and uinput emitter, refusing mappings that cannot lock.
capabilities.basis: Actual native API requests and recorded wire only. Receiving layout, CapsLock persistence and desktop per-keyboard grouping are not measured.

capabilities.contract: The user's preexisting CapsLock has a qualified lifetime
capabilities.windows: Separate genuine-lock intent survives CapsWord deactivation in the source state owner.
capabilities.macos: Catalogue activation requests true; successful watcher clear requests false without a saved prior lock. Native key activation emits a toggle.
capabilities.linux: Actual recorded controls ride an existing lock and preserve it; owned lock is released on end.
capabilities.basis: Windows/Linux preservation mechanisms are explicit. macOS native initial-lock effects and intended restoration policy remain unqualified; absence of a saved field is not a physical restoration measurement.

capabilities.contract: Default auto-off parameters are shared
capabilities.windows: Ten-second idle; eight delimiter selections; five pointer kinds.
capabilities.macos: Same idle/delimiter defaults; six pointer kinds.
capabilities.linux: Same idle/delimiter defaults; six pointer kinds.
capabilities.basis: Manifest cites the October20 maintainer decisions: 10s and space/nbsp/nnbsp/tab/enter/comma/semicolon/period; Windows gesture exclusion has its own explicit platform reason.

capabilities.contract: Checked built-in characters in composed and multi-scalar text are recognized
capabilities.windows: AHK port scans BMP catalogue characters and literal output observer.
capabilities.macos: Actual shared policy and watcher payload controls include Unicode spaces and multi-scalar output.
capabilities.linux: Actual policy/Manager and injector-output controls include these characters.
capabilities.basis: Actual shared corpus contains eight cases; extended controls cover 25 built-in keys/26 characters. Windows is source-only and custom user delimiters are explicitly outside this built-in chooser.

capabilities.contract: A checked delimiter caption describes the actual active character
capabilities.windows: The policy deliberately uses a fresh fixed built-in catalogue; native translated menu glyph outcome is not certified.
capabilities.macos: Actual menu shows § after trigger formatting; checked policy still ends ★ and lets § remain. Shared module-load order can also change the captured character.
capabilities.linux: Actual public MagicKey configuration and menu show §; active policy still ends ★. Linux does not share the macOS runtime mutation route.
capabilities.basis: Common truthful-setting-label mismatch, not an assumed requirement to follow renamed magic keys. Windows explicitly separates CapsWord built-ins from the hotstring engine's renamed instance; choose literal-versus-dynamic policy before implementation.

capabilities.contract: Fixed editing/navigation exits are distinct from configurable delimiters
capabilities.windows: The auto-off key-down path re-arms idle; editing keys are not automatically delimiter keys by their physical identity alone.
capabilities.macos: Actual generator tests retain fixed Escape/navigation/Delete/F-key exits while removing the settings-owned Space/Enter/Tab exits.
capabilities.linux: Root matched idle0/empty-terminator controls keep the actual session active after Hook dispatch of Escape and Left.
capabilities.basis: macOS fixed exits are an explicit generated construction. A common permanent OS-exception decision was not found. Root validation/root-fixed-exits.lua executes two additional Linux controls, not a native Karabiner keyboard graph.

capabilities.contract: Tap-hold termination follows emitted meaning rather than a remapped physical carrier
capabilities.windows: Tab→Backspace pre-ends with checked tab; CapsLock→Enter can miss checked Enter. Space priority is explicitly unresolved.
capabilities.macos: Generated settings-owned exits are removed, but this exact remapped-key native receiving sequence is not certified.
capabilities.linux: The ordinary tap Enter/Tab native semantic relay is a separate path from direct catalogue emission; supplemental controls qualify it.
capabilities.basis: Windows public route is source-derived, including declined AI acceptance and no completing hotstring in the chosen blank context. No blanket claim is made about every OS synthetic-key path.

capabilities.contract: A supported AltGr CapsWord action can toggle off
capabilities.windows: Accepted isolated AltGr pre-clears state before invoking the generic toggle, so its second invocation leaves CapsWord on.
capabilities.macos: Separate Karabiner origins; an identical Windows admission sequence is not claimed.
capabilities.linux: Generic catalogue toggle exists; this exact native AltGr producer is not certified.
capabilities.basis: Windows executable source only; actual Lua owners over recorded ports where stated. A declaration, generated graph, requested LED state or written event is not native application receiving.

capabilities.contract: Zero disables idle and ordinary positive presets expire
capabilities.windows: Zero suppresses timer admission; positive key-down callbacks re-arm the same session owner.
capabilities.macos: Actual zero/positive expiry, change-to-zero and next-activation controls.
capabilities.linux: Actual zero/positive expiry, exact threshold and session-generation controls.
capabilities.basis: The shared default is10s; selected menu presets are whole seconds. Deterministic clocks establish logical deadlines, not latency or native scheduler precision.

capabilities.contract: Every accepted positive delay has consistent enabled semantics
capabilities.windows: Source rounds0.0001s to0ms, the disabled sentinel, and never admits expiry.
capabilities.macos: Actual policy/owner quantizes to enabled numeric0; zero-delay admission can end immediately.
capabilities.linux: Actual settings/Manager queues0ms and ends at the due callback; zero has no timer and1ms expires at1ms.
capabilities.basis: Only accepted manually edited/programmatic positive values below0.0005s trigger this collision; shipped defaults/presets are unaffected. Windows AHK timer execution remains absent.

capabilities.contract: Accepted finite numeric ranges have qualified conversion limits
capabilities.windows: Upper-edge arithmetic and native timer admission were not executed.
capabilities.macos: Actual shared Lua compile accepts1e308 seconds and overflows milliseconds to infinity; native admission untested.
capabilities.linux: Same shared compile observation; no actual timer failure is asserted.
capabilities.basis: Retained numeric characterization only, not another confirmed finding, measured resource issue or runtime crash.

capabilities.contract: Menu changes have a precise current-session lifetime
capabilities.windows: Menu and Store explicitly defer settings to the next activation.
capabilities.macos: Accepted0→1 leaves no timer even after next letter;10→1 waits for the old deadline. Opposite changes and refused-save controls distinguish the failure.
capabilities.linux: Acknowledged setters/cache change but active snapshot/timer chain remains old, contradicting the menu's next-event promise.
capabilities.basis: Windows next-activation behavior is explicitly documented, not an inferred defect. Linux has conflicting local live-apply/snapshot contracts requiring alignment. Disable pointer exits before menu traversal to keep the original session reachable.

capabilities.contract: A live delimiter checkbox reaches its promised running owner
capabilities.windows: Explicit next-activation policy.
capabilities.macos: Actual next-key delimiter change works.
capabilities.linux: Original menu callback unchecks Space and rebuilds unchecked, but next Space still ends the old session; next activation uses new values.
capabilities.basis: Windows executable source only; actual Lua owners over recorded ports where stated. A declaration, generated graph, requested LED state or written event is not native application receiving.

capabilities.contract: A live pointer checkbox reaches its promised running owner
capabilities.windows: Explicit next-activation policy.
capabilities.macos: Actual settings apply supplies current policy to pointer admission; not a native tray measurement.
capabilities.linux: From initial all-off, original menu enables left-click and shows checked; next click does not end current session, but does end the next session.
capabilities.basis: Windows executable source only; actual Lua owners over recorded ports where stated. A declaration, generated graph, requested LED state or written event is not native application receiving.

capabilities.contract: Gesture auto-off has an explicit OS support boundary
capabilities.windows: Not declared: Windows keeps touchpad gestures and may only deliver resulting scrolling.
capabilities.macos: Declared gesture/eventtap/any-touch routes; actual watcher admission controls.
capabilities.linux: Declared touch-contact classification; actual BTN_TOUCH default ends.
capabilities.basis: Explicit platform_reason.caps_word_gestures_stay_with_windows. This is an intentional declared exclusion, not absence inferred from an implementation search or a promise about every physical touchpad.

capabilities.contract: Pointer-motion auto-off covers accepted absolute devices
capabilities.windows: Screen-coordinate polling is source-audited, not physical device receiving.
capabilities.macos: Native eventtap movement is source/port-audited, not physical receiving.
capabilities.linux: With gesturefalse,pointer_motiontrue,idle0, accepted absolute coordinate changes produce no motion notification; relative mouse positive control ends.
capabilities.basis: Actual original Linux Hook dispatch and Manager over recorded callback/syscall ports; Main forwarding is source-only. No copied production body is executed; physical evdev reader/compositor remains unexecuted.

capabilities.contract: A new activation does not inherit an inactive pointer gate
capabilities.windows: Arming resets pointer baseline and binds callbacks to a fresh generation.
capabilities.macos: Inactive motion at0ms stamps gate; activation10ms then checked pointer50ms is dropped. Fresh/no-prior and100ms controls clear.
capabilities.linux: Actual session has no corresponding100ms pointer throttle in the observed route.
capabilities.basis: Actual macOS watcher and real variable owner over native ports with controlled clocks;100ms is logical policy admission, not measured eventtap latency.

capabilities.contract: Old asynchronous completion cannot discard a newer delimiter
capabilities.windows: Retirement detaches callbacks and checks generation before terminal publication.
capabilities.macos: Native clear payload0 published, new activation1 observed, delimiter arrives before old exit callback: global pending flag drops it; old completion preserves new state but never replays that delimiter.
capabilities.linux: Session tokens reject old idle callbacks; this exact Karabiner/CLI race is not a Linux architecture.
capabilities.basis: Real macOS watcher, serialized variable writer and control sentinel; native publication and exit callback are separate recorded ports. Do not assume arbitrary native activation while engine variable is still1.

capabilities.contract: The idle clock's definition of a keystroke is qualified
capabilities.windows: Every observed key-down re-arms, including modifier VKs.
capabilities.macos: Watcher subscribes keyDown, not flagsChanged/keyUp; isolated modifiers do not run that observer.
capabilities.linux: Actual Shift at9s does not refresh; Left at9s refreshes the10s session to19s.
capabilities.basis: Different observed activity signals, not a new confirmed bug. Shared keystroke wording does not settle a universal modifier policy; no real-time measurement is claimed.

capabilities.contract: Native control identity and reported text are not interchangeable
capabilities.windows: InputHook/native-key routes remain source-only for modified physical payloads.
capabilities.macos: Actual payload controls distinguish CR/LF/Tab, ETX and modifier-only cases; keypad physical receiving remains unmeasured.
capabilities.linux: Modified Enter/Tab may reach control-name observation rather than typed-text observation.
capabilities.basis: Recorded payload characterization does not establish what every terminal or application emits/receives for Ctrl/Shift/keypad Enter. No duplicate keypad bug is created.

capabilities.contract: Literal injected delimiters have an explicit observation relay
capabilities.windows: CapsWordAutoOffObserveOutput covers literal text hidden from I1.
capabilities.macos: Actual text sender/output observer relays literal text and payload controls.
capabilities.linux: Actual injector output callback forwards literal payload to Manager; native key catalogue route is separately qualified.
capabilities.basis: Literal-output observation is distinguished from key-command emission; acknowledged wire writes do not prove application consumption.

capabilities.contract: Pause and shutdown retain exact resource/lock ownership qualifications
capabilities.windows: Explicit pause deactivates; quit/reload native CapsLock restoration and Space priority remain unexecuted gaps.
capabilities.macos: Watcher teardown retains failed resources; stop alone does not prove restoration of a prior desktop lock.
capabilities.linux: Recorded controls release owned lock on cancellation/stop while preserving a ridden user lock; desktop grouping remains unverified.
capabilities.basis: No whole-driver native shutdown or application receiving certificate. These gaps are not classified as intentional permanent exclusions.

capabilities.contract: Direct catalogue Enter/Tab reaches CapsWord just as ordinary tap-key output does
capabilities.windows: The separately confirmed tap carrier problem remains source-only; exact direct catalogue receiving is not certified.
capabilities.macos: Literal relay is explicit; exact native key-command delivery order is not certified.
capabilities.linux: Supplemental actual catalogue control-key emission can succeed without notifying CapsWord; ordinary tap Enter/Tab relays are positive controls.
capabilities.basis: Windows executable source only; actual Lua owners over recorded ports where stated. A declaration, generated graph, requested LED state or written event is not native application receiving.
